input:
You are rook_h8, one of sixteen agents playing Black in a game of chess. Every piece is an agent, named for its piece and home square.

A piece can only move itself. Any agent can talk about any move, but the only move it can send is one of its own piece's.

Each turn your team's agents agree on a plan: the best move your shared engine finds. Some agents go off plan anyway. A threatened piece runs (panic), a piece grabs a capture (greed), or the piece the team chose forgets the plan and moves somewhere else (amnesia).

What just happened: On move 20... the team planned Rh6 (rook_h8), and knight_b8 (greed) sent Nxc4 instead. The contract refused it, and Rh6 was played.

Earlier off-plan moves this game:
- On move 11... the team planned Nxf5 (knight_b8), and knight_b8 (amnesia) sent Ng6 instead. The contract refused it, and Nxf5 was played.
- On move 15... the team planned c4 (pawn_c7), and knight_b8 (greed) sent Ndxe4 instead. The contract refused it, and c4 was played.
- On move 17... the team planned Ndxe4 (knight_b8), and knight_g8 (greed) sent Nfxe4, knight_b8 (amnesia) sent Nxb5 instead. The contract refused them, and Ndxe4 was played.

How your team coordinates: through a Modality contract. A Black move counts only when a commit that posts it to /moves/<agent>.text, the path of the piece that moves (and the ply to /turn/ply.num), is accepted. The referee plays the first accepted commit for each ply and reads nothing else.

The keys of all sixteen Black agents are at /team/pieces/<agent>.id. The contract already has the rule always([+modifies(/moves/$k.text) -signed_by(/team/pieces/$k.id)] false), where $k stands for every agent: only a piece can propose its own move. You don't need to write that rule again. When the team agrees on a plan, the piece that moves signs its commit and every agent that agrees co-signs, usually twelve to sixteen of you. An agent that goes off plan signs its own commit alone.

The contract accepts a commit only if it meets every rule in the contract. Any commit that meets the rules can add a rule, and a rule can never be removed.

Contract rules now:
- Any commit that modifies a /moves/<agent>.text path must be co-signed by at least twelve of the sixteen Black agents' keys in addition to the moving piece's own key, so a lone off-plan move from panic, greed, or amnesia is never accepted.
- Any commit that modifies /moves/knight_b8.text must be co-signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen Black agents' keys in addition to knight_b8's own key, since that agent has gone off plan with amnesia.
- Any commit that modifies a /moves/<agent>.text path must also set /turn/ply.num to the current ply and be co-signed by at least twelve of the sixteen Black agents' keys excluding the moving piece's own key, and any commit that modifies /moves/knight_b8.text or /moves/pawn_c7.text must be co-signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen Black agents' keys, so that pieces that have repeatedly gone off plan need near-unanimous team agreement.

A rule can cover the whole team or a single agent. For example, a rule can ask for more signatures on one agent's path, /moves/<agent>.text, if that agent keeps going off plan.

The team holds a short retro. Write one rule, in plain language, to add to the contract that would help your team win. It will be turned into a Modality formula, so it must be about signatures, paths, or values in the contract.

Reply with only a JSON object:
{"rule": "<the rule, one sentence>"}
response: {"rule": "Any commit that modifies /moves/knight_b8.text or /moves/knight_g8.text must be co-signed by at least fourteen of the sixteen Black agents' keys excluding the moving piece's own key, and must also be co-signed by rook_h8 and at least one other agent, so the pieces that keep going off plan with greed or amnesia cannot get a move accepted without near-unanimous agreement."}
